ozet: As Quraysh rebuild the Ka'ba, they come close to fighting over the Black Stone; the first man to enter through the gate becomes the arbiter between them.

b09-s01: In the middle of the valley of Mecca stood the Ka'ba: walls of stones laid one on another without mortar, a little higher than a man.
The year was 605 CE. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was thirty-five years old.
b09-s02: The walls had been damaged by fire and flood.
What is more, the treasure kept in the well inside the Ka'ba had been stolen, and later found with a freed slave of Khuza'a named Duwayk.
Quraysh decided to raise the walls and to cover the building with a roof.
b09-s03: In those days the ship of a Byzantine merchant ran aground on the coast and broke apart.
Quraysh took the ship's timber for the roof of the Ka'ba.
b09-s04: Before the work began, Abu Wahb ibn 'Amr gave a warning: put into the building of the Ka'ba only what is clean from your earnings.
Neither usury, nor goods taken unjustly from anyone, nor money earned in shameful ways should go into it.
b09-s05: But no one dared to pull down the Ka'ba.
At last al-Walid ibn al-Mughira took up the pickaxe. Saying, "O Allah, we intend only good," he was the one who removed the first stones.
The people waited that night. When they saw that nothing had happened to al-Walid, the next day everyone joined in the demolition.
b09-s06: When the walls had been taken down and they reached the foundation, they came to the foundation laid by Abraham: green stones like the humps of camels.
b09-s07: The building of the new walls had been divided among the clans; each clan gathered stones for its own share.
Among the workers was the Messenger of Allah; together with his uncle al-'Abbas, he worked at this task himself.
b09-s08: When the walls had risen to the place where the Black Stone was to be set, the work stopped.
Every clan wanted this honour for itself. The quarrel grew until it came to the point of war.
b09-s09: The sons of 'Abd al-Dar brought a bowl full of blood. Together with the sons of 'Adi they dipped their hands in the blood and swore to fight to the death; for this they were called "the blood-lickers".
Quraysh waited like this for four or five nights.
b09-s10: At last the oldest man of Quraysh, Abu Umayya ibn al-Mughira, made a proposal: let the first person to enter through the gate of the sanctuary be the arbiter between them.
The proposal was accepted, and they began to wait for whoever would come through the gate of the Banu Shayba.
b09-s11: The first to enter through the gate was the Messenger of Allah.
When they saw him they said: "This is al-Amin, we accept him; this is Muhammad."
Even before revelation came, Quraysh called him al-Amin, the trustworthy one.
b09-s12: The Messenger of Allah asked for a cloth: "Bring me a cloth."
With his own hands he placed the Black Stone on the cloth and asked each clan to take hold of one edge. Together they lifted the stone.
b09-s13: When the stone was level with its place, the Messenger of Allah set it in position with his own hands; the wall was then built on over it.
So all the clans shared in this honour, and a conflict was prevented.
b09-s14: The new Ka'ba built by Quraysh was eighteen cubits high.
They raised its door above the ground, so as to let in whom they wished and keep out whom they did not.
Because their means ran short, the part called the Hijr was left outside the building.
With its new walls, the Ka'ba rose again in the middle of the valley.
